text:
Marathon Petroleum edged up 0.89% today to close at $395.93, continuing a strong two-week rally of nearly 9%. The move reflects ongoing volatility in oil markets tied to the Iran conflict: U.S. crude hit $97.26 a barrel today after topping $102 just days ago, and Saudi Arabia's shutdown of a major pipeline following Houthi drone attacks has kept refining margins attractive despite the uncertainty. U.S. refineries are running at 97.8% capacity, near peak levels, which benefits large refiners processing higher oil prices into fuel sales.

The stock's recent strength sits at the intersection of two conflicting signals. Trump's comments about the Iran war ending soon and oil prices falling sharply have triggered profit-taking (the stock dropped $7 on September 10), but geopolitical escalation—Saudi pipeline attacks, Iran's defiant rhetoric—keeps energy markets nervous and supportive of refining stocks that profit when crude prices stay elevated and supply chains are strained.
